mainTopic: The ברכות before קריאת שמע (יוצר אור and אהבה רבה) and the rules and wording of ברכת התורה
overview: The גמרא asks why the morning ברכה says 'יוצר אור ובורא חשך' and mentions darkness instead of the nicer word 'נוגה'. The answer 'we follow the פסוק' falls apart, because we already change 'רע' to 'הכל'. So רבא explains that each ברכה mentions the opposite time: darkness by day, and light at night, as אביי shows from 'גולל אור מפני חשך'. The second morning ברכה is אהבה רבה, though the רבנן in a ברייתא say אהבת עולם. שמואל rules that אהבה רבה can count as ברכת התורה, which leads to a debate about which kinds of learning need that ברכה, from only מקרא up to רבא's view that even תלמוד needs it. Then the גמרא gives several wordings of ברכת התורה and concludes we say them all. Finally, it asks which 'one blessing' the כהנים said in the בית המקדש. שמואל says אהבה רבה, and ריש לקיש's view of יוצר אור turns out to be worked out from his rule that the ברכות do not hold each other back. That reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The opening words of the morning blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of the ברכה of יוצר אור: 'Who forms light and creates darkness.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who forms light and creates darkness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the first morning ברכה before קריאת שמע. It is setting up a question about this wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These words come straight from a פסוק in ישעיהו. Mentioning 'darkness' in a ברכה of praise sounds a little odd, and that is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who forms light' – the name and opening of the first morning ברכה before קריאת שמע
Creates
Darkness

phrases.english: "Who forms light and creates darkness."

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (as the base text for the question that follows)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by quoting the ברכה's wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The morning ברכה opens with 'יוצר אור ובורא חשך', taken from the פסוק in ישעיהו.

steps.title: Why not say a nicer word than darkness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests we should say 'creates brightness' (נוגה) instead of 'creates darkness'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him say: 'Who forms light and creates brightness'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording and suggests replacing 'darkness' with 'brightness'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Darkness has a negative feel, and a ברכה is meant to praise. Saying 'נוגה' (brightness) would avoid mentioning something negative.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him say – a suggestion, here used to push back on the current wording
Brightness, shining light

phrases.english: Let him say: "Who forms light and creates brightness"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברכה of praise should not mention something negative like darkness when a positive word like 'נוגה' is available.

steps.title: We follow the exact words of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we say the ברכה exactly as the פסוק is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: We say it as it is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we keep 'darkness' because that is the word the פסוק uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the ברכה copies the פסוק in ישעיהו word for word, so we don't change it, even if a nicer word exists.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (in the פסוק)
We say

phrases.english: We say it as it is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to the source: the wording follows the פסוק exactly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברכה's words could be freely improved to sound more positive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברכה quotes the פסוק as written, so 'חשך' stays.

steps.title: But we do change the next words of that same verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer: the same פסוק says 'creates evil', yet we change it to 'creates everything' to sound nicer, so we should also change 'darkness' to 'brightness'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the verse also says 'Who makes peace and creates evil' – do we say that as it is written?! Rather, it is written 'evil' and we say 'everything' as a nicer way of speaking. Here too, let us say 'brightness' as a nicer way of speaking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer of step 3 by pointing out that we already change another word in the very same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק continues 'עושה שלום ובורא רע', but the ברכה says 'עושה שלום ובורא את הכל'. So we clearly do not copy the פסוק word for word, and the same polite change should apply to 'חשך'. The challenge stands for now; the גמרא will give a new answer next.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, now… – introduces a strong challenge to the last answer
Evil
Everything
A nicer, more refined way of speaking
Here too

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'כדכתיב' (as it is written) is used here to show the first answer fails: since we already change 'רע' to 'הכל', following the פסוק exactly cannot be the reason we keep 'חשך'.

phrases.english: But if so, "Who makes peace and creates evil":
phrases.notes: This is the next part of the same פסוק in ישעיהו.

phrases.english: do we say it as it is written?!
Rather, it is written "evil"
and we say "everything," as a nicer way of speaking.
phrases.notes: In the ברכה we say 'ובורא את הכל', 'and creates everything'.

phrases.english: Here too, let us say "brightness,"
as a nicer way of speaking!

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא מעתה עושה שלום ובורא רע מי קא אמרינן כדכתיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 3 and brings back the suggestion of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer 'כדכתיב קאמרינן' (we say it as written)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We already change 'רע' to 'הכל' in the same פסוק for politeness, so following the exact wording cannot be the rule; by the same logic 'חשך' should become 'נוגה'.

steps.title: רבא gives a new reason: mention night by day and day by night
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that we say 'creates darkness' so that the morning ברכה also mentions night, and the night ברכה also mentions day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: We say it this way in order to mention the quality of day at night and the quality of night during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier answer ('we say it like the פסוק') did not hold up, so רבא gives a brand-new reason for keeping the word 'darkness.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows the old answer is being dropped. רבא's reason has nothing to do with copying the פסוק. The goal is that each ברכה should mention the opposite time too, so the morning ברכה mentions darkness on purpose. Changing it to 'brightness' would lose that.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Signals that the previous answer is dropped and a new one is coming
The quality or trait of day (light)
The quality or trait of night (darkness)
To mention

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the earlier question was wrong. He agrees we don't just copy the פסוק. He gives a different reason why 'darkness' still belongs in the ברכה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
In order to mention the quality of day at night
and the quality of night during the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that was rejected in step 4 with a new reason for keeping 'darkness.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason replacing a rejected answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think 'darkness' could be changed to 'brightness,' since we already change 'evil' to 'everything.'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Darkness' stays because the morning ברכה is meant to mention night, just as the night ברכה mentions day.

steps.title: Where is day mentioned at night?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that night is mentioned in the morning ('creates darkness'), but asks where day is ever mentioned in the evening ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the quality of night is mentioned during the day, as we say 'Who forms light and creates darkness.' But the quality of day at night, where do you find it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רבא's rule. It agrees the first half works, but it challenges the second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the mentioning goes both ways. In the morning we clearly mention darkness. The גמרא cannot see any mention of light in the night ברכה, so his rule looks only half true.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense that... Used to accept one part before challenging another
As we say
Where do you find it? / How can this be found?

phrases.english: Granted, the quality of night during the day
as we say: "Who forms light and creates darkness,"
but the quality of day at night,
where do you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of רבא's rule from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that day is mentioned at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The evening ברכה seems to have no mention of light, so the 'both ways' rule seems to fail.

steps.title: אביי finds day mentioned in the night ברכה
steps.stepSummary: אביי points to the words 'Who rolls away light before darkness and darkness before light' in the evening ברכה, which mention light at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'Who rolls away light before darkness and darkness before light.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by quoting a line from the evening ברכה that does mention light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The night ברכה talks about light going away and coming back, so it does mention the day. That saves רבא's rule: each ברכה mentions the opposite time.

keyTerms.meaning: Rolls away
Before / in the face of

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule now works both ways: the morning ברכה mentions darkness ('creates darkness'), and the evening ברכה mentions light ('rolls away light before darkness').

phrases.english: Abaye said:
"Who rolls away light before darkness
and darkness before light."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 and defends רבא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to an existing text that fulfills the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The night ברכה seems to have no mention of day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words 'rolls away light before darkness' mention day at night.

steps.title: What is the second morning ברכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on and asks for the wording of the other ברכה said before שמע in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other ברכה, what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The topic of יוצר אור is finished. The גמרא is now setting up a new question about the second ברכה before שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said two ברכות come before שמע in the morning. The first, יוצר אור, has been discussed. Now the גמרא asks how the second one opens.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one
What is it?

phrases.english: And the other one, what is it?
phrases.notes: 'The other one' means the second ברכה we say before שמע in the morning, after יוצר אור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of יוצר אור and opens a new question about the second ברכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The opening wording of the second morning ברכה before שמע.

steps.title: The second ברכה is אהבה רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says the second ברכה is אהבה רבה, and רבי אלעזר taught the same to his son רבי פדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: 'אהבה רבה.' And so too, רבי אלעזר instructed his son רבי פדת to say 'אהבה רבה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the second ברכה begins with אהבה רבה, and a second אמורא's teaching confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's ruling gives the wording. The report about רבי אלעזר teaching his son shows that another אמורא held the same practice. This backs up the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Great love.' The opening words of the second ברכה before שמע
He instructed him / ruled for him
His son

steps.whatToRemember: The two morning ברכות before שמע are יוצר אור, which mentions darkness so night is mentioned by day, and אהבה רבה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
"Great love."
And so too Rabbi Elazar instructed
his son, Rabbi Pedat,
"Great love."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second ברכה is אהבה רבה, as שמואל ruled and as רבי אלעזר taught his son.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports saying אהבה רבה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא backs up the previous step: the ברכה is אהבה רבה, not אהבת עולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: we do not say 'An eternal love.' We say 'An abounding love.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the second morning ברכה is אהבה רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, אמוראים said the ברכה is אהבה רבה. Now the גמרא shows that an earlier source, a ברייתא, says the same thing. It even rejects the other wording, אהבת עולם, by name.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a supporting source)
'An eternal love', one possible opening of the ברכה
'An abounding (great) love', the other possible opening

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
We do not say "An eternal love,"
but rather "An abounding love."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 9 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the second ברכה is אהבה רבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says not to say אהבת עולם but אהבה רבה

steps.title: The רבנן say אהבת עולם, based on a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן in the same ברייתא disagree and say the ברכה is אהבת עולם, because a פסוק uses that phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say: 'An eternal love.' And so the פסוק says: 'With an eternal love I have loved you; therefore I have drawn you with kindness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion: the רבנן hold that the ברכה should say אהבת עולם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן base their wording on the language of a נביא, who describes ה׳'s love as אהבת עולם. So the ברייתא contains two opinions, not just one. The question of wording stays a real disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
And so it says, introducing a פסוק as support
I have drawn you with kindness

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא only supports אהבה רבה. The same ברייתא also brings the רבנן, who say אהבת עולם, so both wordings have a source.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say "An eternal love,"
and so it says:
"And with an eternal love I have loved you;
therefore I have drawn you with kindness."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, the ברכה opens with אהבת עולם, following the language of the פסוק in ירמיהו.

steps.title: אהבה רבה can cover ברכת התורה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that someone who learns before שמע needs ברכת התורה, but after שמע he is already covered by אהבה רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If someone got up early to learn Torah, then before he says קריאת שמע he must say a ברכה. Once he has said קריאת שמע, he does not need to, because אהבה רבה already covered him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule about אהבה רבה. This ברכה is strong enough to count as ברכת התורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהבה רבה praises ה׳ for giving us the Torah and asks to understand and learn it. Because of this, saying it works like saying ברכת התורה. So it matters whether a person learns before or after davening שמע and its ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Got up early to learn
He must say a ברכה (here, ברכת התורה)
Exempted, already covered

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that אהבה רבה can take the place of ברכת התורה. It comes up in practical הלכה when someone forgot to say ברכת התורה in the morning.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
If someone got up early to learn,
as long as he has not yet said Shema,
he must say a blessing.
phrases.notes: The ברכה meant here is ברכת התורה, the ברכה said before learning.

phrases.english: Once he has said Shema,
he does not need to say a blessing,
because he was already covered by "An abounding love."
phrases.notes: אהבה רבה talks about ה׳ giving us the Torah, so it does the job of ברכת התורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הִשְׁכִּים לִשְׁנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the identification of אהבה רבה to give a new הלכה about ברכת התורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning before קריאת שמע needs ברכת התורה. After קריאת שמע it does not, because אהבה רבה already covered it.

steps.title: רב הונא: only מקרא needs a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says learning פסוקים needs a ברכה, but learning מדרש does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: For learning מקרא (the written פסוקים), one must say a ברכה. For מדרש, one does not need to say a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just talked about ברכת התורה, it now asks which kinds of Torah learning need that ברכה. רב הונא gives the narrowest view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב הונא, only the written words of the תורה themselves need a ברכה. Learning laws drawn out of the פסוקים does not count for this ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The written תורה, the פסוקים themselves
Learning laws drawn out from the פסוקים

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
For Scripture, one must say a blessing,
and for midrash, one does not need to say a blessing.
phrases.notes: מדרש here means learning the הלכות that come out of the פסוקים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לַמִּקְרָא צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from when ברכת התורה is needed to what kind of learning needs it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקרא needs a ברכה; מדרש does not.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: מקרא and מדרש need a ברכה, משנה does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר widens the rule: מקרא and מדרש both need a ברכה, but משנה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: For מקרא and for מדרש one must say a ברכה. For משנה one does not need to say a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר disagrees with רב הונא and includes מדרש in the learning that needs a ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדרש is tied to the פסוקים, so רבי אלעזר treats it like the written תורה. משנה is a list of rulings without the פסוקים, so in his view it does not need a ברכה. The argument is still open, and the גמרא will bring more opinions next.

keyTerms.meaning: The rulings of the תנאים, stated without the פסוקים
He does not need to say a ברכה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
For Scripture and for midrash, one must say a blessing;
for Mishnah, one does not need to say a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: לַמִּקְרָא וְלַמִּדְרָשׁ צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא by adding מדרש to the learning that needs a ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקרא and מדרש need a ברכה; משנה does not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: משנה also needs a blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says משנה also needs ברכת התורה, but תלמוד does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even for משנה you must make a ברכה, but for תלמוד you do not need to make a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives his opinion on which kinds of learning need ברכת התורה. רבי יוחנן adds משנה to the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said only מקרא and מדרש need a ברכה, not משנה. רבי יוחנן goes one step further and includes משנה too. He still draws a line at תלמוד, which explains the reasons behind the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The short, organized rulings of the תנאים
Learning that explains the reasons behind the משנה
Even... also; adds something to a list
One must make a ברכה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even for Mishnah, too, one must make a blessing
but for Talmud, one does not need to make a blessing.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף לַמִּשְׁנָה נָמֵי צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens רבי אלעזר's rule from step 14 to include משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקרא, מדרש and משנה need ברכת התורה; תלמוד does not.

steps.title: רבא: even תלמוד needs a blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even תלמוד needs ברכת התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Even for תלמוד you must make a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the widest opinion of all: every kind of Torah learning, including תלמוד, needs a ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opinions keep growing: first only פסוקים, then מדרש, then משנה, and now רבא includes תלמוד too. With this view, there is no kind of Torah learning left without a ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: To go back and bless again

steps.whyThisMatters: This widest view is the one the גמרא backs up in the next step, so it is the strongest opinion in this list.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Even for Talmud one must
make a blessing.
phrases.notes: Some versions say "go back and bless" (round brackets); the corrected wording just says "bless" (square brackets).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: אַף לַתַּלְמוּד צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes past רבי יוחנן's limit and includes תלמוד as well.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All Torah learning, even תלמוד, needs ברכת התורה.

steps.title: רב would bless before teaching his students
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי tells how רב washed his hands and made a ברכה before teaching, which supports רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב חייא בר אשי said: Many times I stood before רב to learn our chapter in the ספרא of the school of רב. He would first wash his hands, make a ברכה, and then teach us our chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about what רב actually did, as support for רבא's view that even deep learning needs a ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב taught the ספרא with full explanations, so his lesson was like learning תלמוד. Since he still made a ברכה first, this shows that תלמוד-style learning needs a ברכה, just as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Many times
The ספרא, the מדרש on ויקרא, from the school of רב
Our chapter
Washed his hands
Taught us

phrases.english: For Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said:
Many times
I would stand before Rav
to learn our chapter
in the "Sifra of the school of Rav,"
he would first wash his hands,
and make a blessing,
and teach us our chapter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רבא's view from step 16 with a story about רב.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that even תלמוד needs a ברכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's practice, reported by his student רב חייא בר אשי, of making a ברכה before teaching the ספרא with explanations.

steps.title: What is the wording of the blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what words one says in ברכת התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What ברכה does he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next step by asking what the ברכה actually says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about when you need the ברכה. Now the question changes to what the ברכה says, so the גמרא starts a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: What blessing does he say?

phrases.english: What does he bless?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving a ברכה is needed, it asks what that ברכה says.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording of ברכת התורה.

steps.title: שמואל: Who commanded us to engage in Torah
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives the wording: אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו לעסוק בדברי תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The ברכה is "Who made us holy with His מצוות and commanded us to engage in words of Torah."
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by giving the wording of the ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה follows the usual pattern of a ברכה on a מצוה: "Who made us holy with His מצוות and commanded us." The מצוה named here is לעסוק בדברי תורה, being busy with Torah, and not just reading it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who made us holy with His commandments
And commanded us
To engage, be busy, in words of Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The opinions grow step by step: פסוקים, then מדרש, then משנה, and רבא says even תלמוד needs ברכת התורה, backed by רב's practice. שמואל's wording is "לעסוק בדברי תורה."

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
"Who sanctified us with His commandments
and commanded us to engage in words of Torah."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ לַעֲסוֹק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברכה is: אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו לעסוק בדברי תורה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ending for the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds an ending to ברכת התורה. It asks that Torah be sweet to us and to our children, and it closes with המלמד תורה לעמו ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן finishes the blessing like this: "Please, ה׳ our God, make the words of Your Torah sweet in our mouths and in the mouths of Your people Israel. May we, our children, and the children of all Your people Israel all know Your name and learn Your Torah. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who teaches Torah to His people Israel."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still answering the question 'what do we say for ברכת התורה?' Here רבי יוחנן gives the ending he adds to the blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gave only the opening words, לעסוק בדברי תורה. רבי יוחנן adds a request that Torah be sweet and that it be passed on to future generations. He then closes with a חתימה, a 'ברוך אתה ה׳' ending.

keyTerms.meaning: concludes it, adds an ending to it
please make sweet (pleasant)
our descendants
Who teaches Torah

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan concludes it this way:
"Please make sweet, ה׳ our God,
the words of Your Torah in our mouths
and in the mouths of Your people, the house of Israel,
and may we and our descendants
and the descendants of Your people, the house of Israel,
all of us, be those who know Your name and those who engage in Your Torah.

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ הַמְלַמֵּד תּוֹרָה לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל״.
phrases.english: Blessed are You, ה׳, Who teaches Torah to His people Israel."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an ending to the opening wording שמואל gave in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What words are said in ברכת התורה (step 18).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After the opening, add הערב נא and close with המלמד תורה לעמו ישראל.

steps.title: רב המנונא's version of the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא gives a different ברכת התורה. It thanks ה׳ for choosing us and giving us the Torah, and it closes with נותן התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said the blessing is: "Who chose us from all the nations and gave us His Torah. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who gives the Torah."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more answer to 'what do we say for ברכת התורה?' This time it is a short blessing from רב המנונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's version is a request for sweetness and for the next generations. רב המנונא's version is thanks: ה׳ chose us and gave us His Torah. It is a separate blessing with its own חתימה.

keyTerms.meaning: Who chose us
from all the nations
Giver of the Torah

phrases.english: And Rav Hamnuna said:
"Who chose us from all the nations
and gave us His Torah.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Giver of the Torah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, different wording, alongside שמואל's and רבי יוחנן's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What words are said in ברכת התורה (step 18).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אשר בחר בנו מכל העמים ונתן לנו את תורתו, ending with נותן התורה.

steps.title: רב המנונא praises this blessing as the finest
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says his blessing, אשר בחר בנו, is the finest of the ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: This is the finest of the blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא gives his opinion about the blessing he just taught. He says it is the best of all the ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is praise, not a new wording. רב המנונא is saying that his short ברכה, which thanks ה׳ for choosing us and giving us the Torah, stands out among the ברכות. The next step decides that we say all the versions together.

keyTerms.meaning: the finest, the most excellent
among the blessings

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
This is the finest of the blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: זוֹ הִיא מְעוּלָּה שֶׁבַּבְּרָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Praises the blessing given in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשר בחר בנו is the finest of the ברכות.

steps.title: Conclusion: say all the versions
steps.stepSummary: Since there are several versions of ברכת התורה, the גמרא concludes that we say all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, let us say all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the discussion about the wording of ברכת התורה. Instead of picking one version, it tells us to say them all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not treat the versions as arguing with each other. They can all be said together: לעסוק בדברי תורה, then הערב נא, then אשר בחר בנו.

keyTerms.meaning: therefore
let us say all of them

steps.whatToRemember: ברכת התורה is made of all three pieces: שמואל's opening (לעסוק בדברי תורה), רבי יוחנן's הערב נא, and רב המנונא's אשר בחר בנו. We say them all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the morning ברכות התורה in our סידור include all three of these texts.

phrases.english: Therefore, let us say all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines all the versions given in steps 19 to 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All the versions of ברכת התורה are said.

steps.title: The משנה about the כהנים' morning blessings in the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת תמיד. The כהנים said one blessing, read the עשרת הדברות and the three parts of קריאת שמע, and blessed the people with three blessings. On שבת they added a blessing for the outgoing משמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: The appointed one told the כהנים, "Say one blessing!" They said it. Then they read the Ten Commandments, שמע, והיה אם שמוע, and ויאמר. They blessed the people with three blessings: אמת ויציב, עבודה, and ברכת כהנים. On שבת they added one more blessing for the group of כהנים that was finishing its week.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about what the כהנים said each morning in the בית המקדש. This sets up the next question: what was that 'one blessing'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to the larger subject of the ברכות around קריאת שמע. The משנה says the כהנים said only 'one blessing' before שמע, but it does not say which one. That missing detail is what the גמרא will examine next.

keyTerms.meaning: the appointed one, the כהן in charge
the Ten Commandments
the blessing after שמע about redemption
the blessing asking ה׳ to accept the קרבנות
a group of כהנים serving in the בית המקדש for a week

steps.confusionAlert: 'One blessing' here is said by the כהנים before קריאת שמע. It is not ברכת כהנים, which is listed separately among the three blessings for the people.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת תמיד, about the daily routine in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: The appointed one said to them:
"Recite one blessing!"
And they recited the blessing.
And they read the Ten Commandments,
שמע, והיה אם שמוע, and ויאמר.
And they blessed the people with three blessings:
אמת ויציב, עבודה, and ברכת כהנים.
And on Shabbat they add one blessing
for the outgoing watch.
phrases.notes: The groups of כהנים switched on שבת, so the group finishing its week got a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ברכת התורה back to the ברכות around קריאת שמע, through a משנה about the בית המקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the בית המקדש, the כהנים said one blessing, read the עשרת הדברות and קריאת שמע, blessed the people with אמת ויציב, עבודה and ברכת כהנים, and on שבת added a blessing for the outgoing משמר.

steps.title: What is the one blessing the כהנים said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'one blessing' in the משנה means. It tells a story where great rabbis could not answer the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'one blessing'? It is like the time רבי אבא and רבי יוסי בר אבא came to a certain place. The people asked them what 'one blessing' meant, and they did not know. They went and asked רב מתנה, and he did not know either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which blessing the כהנים said in the משנה from תמיד. It tells a story to show that this question was hard. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says 'one blessing' and never names it. The story shows that even רבי אבא, רבי יוסי בר אבא, and רב מתנה did not have an answer ready. That makes the answer that comes next more important.

keyTerms.meaning: One blessing, the words from the משנה in תמיד
They happened to come to a place
They did not have it in hand; they did not know the answer
They asked him

phrases.english: What is "one blessing"?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Like that incident where Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Yosei bar Abba
happened to come to a certain place,
the people asked them: What is "one blessing"?
They did not have the answer at hand.
So they came and asked Rav Mattana,
and he did not have the answer at hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the unclear words 'one blessing' mean in the משנה quoted in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which blessing the כהנים said as their 'one blessing' before קריאת שמע.

steps.title: שמואל says the blessing was אהבה רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers in the name of שמואל: the one blessing was אהבה רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came and asked רב יהודה. He told them: this is what שמואל said, 'אהבה רבה.'
steps.whatsHappening: Finally someone has an answer. רב יהודה quotes his teacher שמואל: the blessing was אהבה רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהבה רבה is the second blessing before שמע, and it speaks about ה׳'s love and the Torah. According to שמואל, that is the blessing the כהנים said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Great love,' the second blessing before קריאת שמע
This is what he said

phrases.english: They came and asked Rav Yehuda.
He said to them: This is what Shmuel said:
"An abounding love."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The one blessing was אהבה רבה, according to שמואל.

steps.title: ריש לקיש says the blessing was יוצר אור
steps.stepSummary: A second answer, quoted in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש, says the one blessing was יוצר אור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי אמי, who said it in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: it was 'יוצר אור.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer. In the name of ריש לקיש, the one blessing was יוצר אור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוצר אור is the first blessing before שמע, about ה׳ creating light. Now there are two opinions: אהבה רבה from שמואל and יוצר אור from ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who forms light,' the first blessing before קריאת שמע

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Zerika said that Rabbi Ami said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: ״יוֹצֵר אוֹר״.
phrases.english: that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: "Who forms light."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 25, different from שמואל in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The one blessing was יוצר אור, according to ריש לקיש.

steps.title: ריש לקיש never said it outright; it was worked out
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף reveals that ריש לקיש never said 'יוצר אור' outright. People figured it out from a different statement of his: the ברכות do not hold each other back.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said: what רבי זריקא said was not said outright. It was worked out from something else. רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי אמי, in the name of ריש לקיש: 'This shows that the ברכות do not hold each other back.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר יוסף corrects how ריש לקיש's teaching was passed on. The words 'יוצר אור' were not ריש לקיש's own words. People drew them out of another rule he taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's actual statement was about the משנה in general: the ברכות of שמע do not hold each other back. That means saying one of them without the other still counts. People then concluded that he must have held the כהנים said יוצר אור. So the ruling of 'יוצר אור' is only a conclusion drawn from his words, not something he said.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said outright, in so many words
It was worked out from a more general statement
This shows; we can learn from here
They do not hold each other back; missing one does not cancel the other

steps.confusionAlert: רב יצחק בר יוסף is not saying the answer 'יוצר אור' is wrong. He is only saying that ריש לקיש did not say it outright; it was figured out from his other statement.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר,
phrases.english: When Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef came, he said:
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל and brought the more exact version of the teaching.

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּרַבִּי זְרִיקָא לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִתְּמַר
phrases.english: That teaching of Rabbi Zerika was not said outright,
rather it was worked out from a general statement.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: For Rabbi Zerika said that Rabbi Ami said
that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת בְּרָכוֹת אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ.
phrases.english: This shows that the blessings do not hold each other back.
phrases.notes: 'This' means the משנה in תמיד, where the כהנים said only one blessing before שמע instead of the usual two.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּרַבִּי זְרִיקָא לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִתְּמַר אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects how the ריש לקיש teaching in step 27 was passed on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that ריש לקיש said 'יוצר אור' outright, not the answer itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The quote was passed on as ריש לקיש's own words, but it was only a conclusion drawn from his general rule that the ברכות do not hold each other back.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'ברכות אין מעכבות זו את זו' matters in practice. Someone who said only one of the ברכות before שמע still gets credit for the one he said.

steps.title: How ריש לקיש's rule points to יוצר אור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to show how people concluded יוצר אור. If the כהנים said יוצר אור, that fits ריש לקיש's rule, since they skipped אהבה רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say they used to say 'יוצר אור.' That is why the ברכות do not hold each other back, since they did not say 'אהבה רבה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to explain how people got from ריש לקיש's rule to the answer 'יוצר אור.' It shows that the יוצר אור reading fits his rule well, and it is setting up a comparison with the other possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהנים said only יוצר אור, then they left out אהבה רבה, which comes after it. Their blessing still counted, so the ברכות must not hold each other back. The word 'בשלמא' tells us the גמרא is about to ask how this would work if they had said אהבה רבה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say... (sets up a contrast with the other option)
That is why; that explains
They used to say

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא ״יוֹצֵר אוֹר״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי,
phrases.english: It works well if you say they used to say "Who forms light";

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דִּבְרָכוֹת אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ,
phrases.english: that is why the blessings do not hold each other back,
since they did not say "An abounding love."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא ״יוֹצֵר אוֹר״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the conclusion described in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That ריש לקיש held the כהנים' one blessing was יוצר אור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His rule that the ברכות do not hold each other back fits well if the כהנים said יוצר אור and skipped אהבה רבה.
